newsitem.title: RUSSIA: St Petersburg to build new airport terminal.
newsitem.headline: St Petersburg to build new airport terminal.

text.p: Construction of a new international passenger terminal at St Petersburg airport will begin early in 1997 and take two years, a senior official said.
Executive director of St Petersburg international airport Sergei Gulnitsky told Reuters the city hoped for a credit from the Europen Bank for Reconstruction and Development.

"At the end of December the board of directors of the EBRD will meet to decide whether to grant a $75 million credit. At the beginning of next year we will be able to begin construction," Gulnitsky said,

He said the total cost of the terminal, to be named Pulkovo-3 would be $140 million. He said Deutsche Morgan Grenfell and U.S. Overseas Private Investment Corporation (OPIC) would also partcipate in the financing.
Gulnitsky also said Pulkovo-3 would be built to international standards ant it would have an annual capacity of three million passengers.
He said it would be linked with Pulkovo's existing terminals. However, runways and other facilities would not be expanded.
"Pulkovo can handle 50 million passengers annually," he said.
